item.dc:creator: Owen Harrington Department of Geography, The Pennsylvania State University, USAOWEN HARRINGTON is a PhD Candidate in the Department of Geography at Pennsylvania State University, University Park, PA 16802. E-mail: ofh5033@psu.edu. His research interests include the histories of fossil fuel production and environmental justice in Appalachia, the role of the fossil fuel sector in clean energy transitions, and geographies of waste production, among others.

item.dc:creator: Oscar Wycisk Francis Markham Marnie O’Bryan a Centre for Indigenous Policy Research, POLIS: The Centre for Social Research, The Australian National University, Australiab Batchelor Institute, Australiac Graduate School of Education, The University of Melbourne, AustraliaOSCAR WYCISK is a PhD Candidate at the Centre for Indigenous Policy Research, POLIS: The Centre for Social Research, The Australian National University, Canberra, Australia. E-mail: oscar.wycisk@anu.edu.au. His research interest focuses on the political economy of education policy, particularly as it affects the opportunities available to remote living Aboriginal students in the Northern Territory of Australia.FRANCIS MARKHAM is an ARC DECRA Fellow at the Centre for Indigenous Policy Research, POLIS: The Centre for Social Research, The Australian National University, Canberra, Australia. E-mail: francis.markham@anu.edu.au. Francis’s research applies critical geographical thought to public policy questions.MARNIE O’BRYAN is an Adjunct Associate Professor at the Batchelor Institute, Darwin, Northern Territory, Australia and Honorary Fellow at the Graduate School of Education, The University of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. E-mail: obryan.marnie@gmail.com. Marnie’s research centers on First Nations policy in Australia, with a special interest in equity in education for First Nations youth.
